title: Add multiscale fingerprint quarantine guard for gradual regressions
author: Anika Shah
description:
Context and motivation: We frequently see gradual-performance degradations that slip past point-estimate canaries because the signal is distributed across multiple traffic phases and timescales. This PR introduces a multiscale fingerprint quarantine guard that: (1) builds phase-aware traffic fingerprints at multiple temporal granularities, (2) detects divergence across scales using a robust similarity metric, and (3) applies progressive quarantine controls that throttle or isolate suspect traffic slices during rollouts.

Design summary: The guard computes per-route phase fingerprints (startup, steady-state, tail) using stratified quantile histograms for latency and throughput features. Fingerprints are kept at 5s, 1m, and 15m aggregation windows and compared to a rolling baseline using cosine similarity + Kullback-Leibler smoothing for distribution drift. When sustained divergence is detected at the mid and long scales but not at the finest scale (indicating slow drift rather than transient spikes), the guard triggers a progressive quarantine: first divert 10% of canary traffic to a spectator pool, then pause new canaries for the route and escalate to automatic rollback if divergence exceeds thresholds for 30m.

What this changes: - New guard implementation and registration (canary/guards/multiscale_quarantine_guard.py) - Telemetry: adds multiscale_fingerprint.* metrics and event annotation (metrics/telemetry_schema.yaml) - Canary evaluator integration points and config knobs for thresholds and quarantine policies (canary/configs/multiscale_guard.yaml) - Unit + integration tests and a small synthetic traffic generator used for local validation (tests/perf/multiscale_guard_test.py, tests/perf/synthetic_traffic.py)

Testing and validation: Local unit tests, integration tests against the perf-canary harness, and a staging week-long replay of 72 hours of production traces with injected slow drift patterns. We observed earlier detection (median lead time +18 minutes) compared to baseline percentile-only canaries and zero false positives on the replay dataset. CI runs: full test matrix and telemetry linting passed on the final push.

Rollout plan: Feature flag behind canary.guard.multiscale_quarantine. Start with shadow mode for two weeks on <staging> then enable soft quarantine for low-risk routes (10% traffic diversion) and expand to more aggressive policies only after SRE sign-off. The PR includes doc notes and an ops runbook (docs/ops/multiscale_quarantine_runbook.md) describing thresholds, troubleshooting queries, and rollback steps.

release_notes: Adds a multiscale fingerprint quarantine guard to canary evaluator. Detects gradual distributional regressions across multiple time scales and applies progressive quarantine controls to protect production traffic. Feature gated behind canary.guard.multiscale_quarantine.
notes_for_ops: Runbook available at docs/ops/multiscale_quarantine_runbook.md. Key dashboards: multiscale_fingerprint.similarity, multiscale_quarantine.active_routes, multiscale_quarantine.divergence_seconds. Default soft quarantine diverts 10% traffic and is reversible via feature flag.
